title: The Supervisory Interview: Purpose and Mindset
summary: Why supervisors interview, how supervisory interviews differ from enforcement interviews and recruitment interviews, and how mindset shapes what the interviewer hears.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why supervisors interview, how supervisory interviews differ from enforcement interviews and recruitment interviews, and how mindset shapes what the interviewer hears.
Learning Objectives: Explain the role of interviews in risk assessment, inspections and governance reviews
Distinguish supervisory from enforcement interviews and their evidential standards
Recognise how assumptions and mindset affect an interview
Syllabus: Interviews in the supervisory cycle: inspections, reviews and fitness and propriety
Supervisory versus enforcement interviews: purpose, powers and safeguards
Introducing a PEACE-style structure for supervisory interviews
The right supervisory perspective: curious, sceptical and fair
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors who conduct on-site visits, thematic reviews and governance assessments
Staff assessing fitness and propriety of directors and senior managers, including authorisation teams
Team leaders who plan inspections and review interview evidence before findings are issued
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of on-site inspections or firm engagement is helpful. No prior interview training is required.
Core Reading: Rebecca Milne and Ray Bull, Investigative Interviewing: Psychology and Practice (1999)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
